articles.body: LR Publishes Alternative Fuel Retrofit Guidelines Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 15, 2026 The bow of a large cargo ship in dry dock. Image by jaslagman0 from Pixabay Lloyd’s Register (LR) has published new Guidance Notes for Retrofit of Alternative Fuels and Energy Saving Devices highlighting the growing complexity of ship retrofit projects. As regulatory and commercial pressures increase through measures such as FuelEU Maritime, the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and the IMO’s greenhouse gas reduction ambitions, retrofitting existing vessels is becoming an increasingly important pathway for owners seeking to improve efficiency, reduce emissions and extend asset life. However, the challenge is no longer simply selecting a single fuel or technology. Retrofit projects have become increasingly complex, requiring careful consideration of fuel storage, engine compatibility, safety systems, crew training, statutory approvals, vessel design and long-term operational impacts. To help the industry navigate these challenges, LR’s new publication brings together alternative fuels and energy-saving devices within a single retrofit framework. It covers the practical considerations associated with converting vessels to LNG, methanol, ethanol, ammonia, hydrogen and LPG, alongside the installation of wind-assisted propulsion systems (WAPS) and air lubrication systems (ALS). A central theme is that many retrofit decisions must be made much earlier in the process than owners may expect. Factors such as engine conversion capability, available onboard space, tank location, fuel-system integration and project execution can have a major influence on project costs, timelines and operational outcomes. The guidance emphasizes the importance of early collaboration between owners, shipyards, equipment manufacturers, flag administrations and classification societies to avoid delays and reduce project risk. The publication also highlights growing opportunities for energy-saving technologies. Wind-assisted propulsion systems, for example, can benefit from incentives under FuelEU Maritime through a reward factor designed to recognize their contribution to lowering greenhouse gas intensity At the same time, the guidance notes reflect growing industry recognition that retrofit projects must address both technical and human factors. Extensive crew training, revised operating procedures, updated safety management systems and new risk assessments are identified as essential elements of successful deployment, particularly for fuels such as ammonia and hydrogen, which introduce new safety considerations The Guidance Notes for Retrofit of Alternative Fuels and Energy Saving Devices is available from LR’s Retrofit Research program: Ship Retrofitting | Retrofit Research Programme | LR

articles.title: Minesto reports 'record' 48-hour service intervention on its tidal power plant
articles.summary: Minesto has performed a service intervention on its Dragon 4 tidal power plant in record time, carrying out the recovery, inspection, and...
articles.body: Marine Energy October 15, 2026 · 18 hours ago Minesto reports 'record' 48-hour service intervention on its tidal power plant NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Minesto Minesto has performed a service intervention on its Dragon 4 tidal power plant in record time, carrying out the recovery, inspection, and redeployment offshore process in 48 hours, the Swedish ocean energy developer reported today, October 15. Minesto revealed that, after years of improving the process, it had achieved its fastest turnaround to date, with a complete service intervention of a Dragon 4 power plant performed within 48 hours in Vestmannasund, Faroe Islands. The intervention included recovery, extraction of the nacelle for inspection of the upgraded generator following its first ten weeks of operation, maintenance activities, reassembly, quality and functional checks, and redeployment offshore. The work was carried out during a low-production tidal period. Minesto "The ability to complete a full service operation and return the system to power production in only 48 hours demonstrates a key competitive advantage of our technology," said Martin Edlund , Minesto's CEO. "High performance is important, but equally important is the ability to maintain the system cost efficiently. Notably, our method does not rely on sophisticated and expensive infrastructure, making it suitable for remote locations and areas of the world without port infrastructure and access to advanced marine engineering capabilities." Minesto notes that the central feature of the concept is the ability to swap subsystems, such as the nacelle, during short intervention campaigns. By using spare modules, more extensive inspections, maintenance activities and upgrades can be performed onshore without impact on availability and energy yield. This capability becomes increasingly valuable as we move towards larger commercial deployments and multi-unit installations," said Bernt Erik Westre , CTO of Minesto. articles.title: Seven Sailors Missing as Drones Strike Tankers Near Romania
articles.summary: Rescuers were searching for seven missing crew on Thursday from one of two chemical tankers that caught fire overnight just outside Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea, after Russian drones strayed into national airspace, Romanian officials said.

Romanian Interior Ministry/Handout via REUTERS BUCHAREST, Oct 15 (Reuters) – Rescuers searched on Thursday for seven missing sailors after drones struck two chemical tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze and raising fresh security concerns along a vital shipping route used by Ukraine. Romanian President Nicusor Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones but declined to say whether Russia was responsible, while a NATO military source said the drones came from Russia. “The drones that caused the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the NATO source said. The two vessels were anchored near the mouth of the Sulina canal leading into the Danube River, a major export route used by Ukraine as Russia has repeatedly attacked Ukraine’s Black Sea ports. One was inside Romanian territorial waters and the other just outside. The missing crew were among 12 sailors aboard the San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader, which was hit 13 nautical miles southeast of the Sulina canal, one mile outside Romanian waters. Five crew members were rescued, Romanian officials said. The second vessel, the Comoros-flagged chemical and oil tanker Yara J, caught fire after being struck 8-10 miles southeast of Sulina inside Romanian waters late on Wednesday. All crew were safe. The attacks are the latest in a series of strikes on commercial shipping in the western Black Sea. At least five other cargo vessels have been hit near the coasts of Romania and neighboring NATO member Bulgaria over the past 10 days, with at least 23 sailors reported missing or dead. Those attacks occurred outside NATO territorial waters. “The situation in the Black Sea is serious,” Romania’s Dan said. “Commercial ships are being attacked and sunk. Seafarers killed, injured, and missing, very close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria. Lives, global trade, and critical infrastructure are at stake.” The interior ministry said it had sent two Black Hawk helicopters to the search and rescue mission, as well as two ships with medical staff on board. “At the moment, the rescue cannot be done safely because of very big waves,” it said in a statement. NATO said in a statement it was in contact with Romanian officials. It added two other vessels had been targeted in the Black Sea overnight, Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny inside Romanian waters and Tanzanian-flagged tanker Dania J, moored in the Ukrainian Danube port of Izmail. It did not mention casualties. “NATO will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defense posture as needed,” NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said after meeting Dan and Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Thursday. Romania shares a 614-km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube, and has repeatedly reported Russian drone incursions into its airspace since the start of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The escalating attacks on Black Sea shipping have heightened concerns over grain exports from the region. Russian attacks on Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports have forced Kyiv to rely increasingly on Danube ports and shipping routes close to the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria. Ukraine, for its part, has targeted Russian vessels near the mouth of the Don River in the Azov Sea. Bulgaria’s Radev said EU leaders would discuss a proposed moratorium on attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea. “We’re looking at the Black Sea as a global food artery,” Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu told a security conference in Warsaw earlier this week. “It is currently, unfortunately, the deadliest sea when it comes to the number of casualties of sailors in the last months. That means we need to increase our investments in deterrence, defense.” (Reporting by Luiza Ilie, additional reporting by Sabine Siebold; Editing by Alexandra Hudson, Toby Chopra and Ros Russell) (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026. articles.summary: Oil & gas exploration player Finder Energy has awarded Japanese ENEOS Drilling a contract to provide a semi-submersible drilling rig for the...
articles.body: Project & Tenders October 15, 2026 · 19 hours ago Rig provider and other contractors revealed for Timor-Leste's oil field NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Hakuryu-5 semi-submersible rig. Source: ENEOS Drilling Oil & gas exploration player Finder Energy has awarded Japanese ENEOS Drilling a contract to provide a semi-submersible drilling rig for the development of its offshore oil field in Timor-Leste. ENEOS Drilling's Hakuryu-5 semi-submersible drilling unit will perform the drilling campaign at the Kuda Tasi and Jahal (KTJ) project, including three firm development wells, with options for two additional wells. The Japanese player will also provide the associated equipment and personnel. The contract is conditional upon receipt of the required joint venture, government and Finder board approvals by December 31, 2026, together with ENEOS parent company and board approvals by November 16, 2026. The campaign will begin on December 1, 2027, and has an estimated duration of approximately 150 days to drill and complete the wells for production, including running completion assemblies and installation of the wellheads and Christmas Trees ready for hook-up to the Petrojarl I FPSO. "Securing the Hakuryu-5 is a major milestone for the KTJ Project which brings us a step closer to FID and providing clear visibility on the timing of the development drilling program," said Damon Neaves , Finder Energy CEO. "This is also a strong signal of the progress being made towards delivering Timor-Leste's next offshore oil development." According to Finder Energy, the two optional drilling slots provide flexibility to accommodate participation by other operators or to undertake exploration or appraisal drilling targeting potential tie-back opportunities within PSC 19-11. As for other contractors selected for the project, Finder Energy reported that Sumitomo will manufacture, supply and deliver oil country tubular goods (OCTG) including casing, production liner and completion tubing, three Christmas Trees are under fabrication by OneSubsea , and that wellheads have been acquired from another joint venture. AGR will provide integrated drilling management services to support the planning, management and execution of the development drilling program on behalf of Finder, with Finder retaining overall responsibility as operator, and SLB will supply upper completion equipment for the development wells, including downhole flow-control valves, gauges, chemical-injection equipment, packers, subsurface safety valves, control lines, cables, protectors, splices, contingencies and spares. The final investment decision (FID) for the project is anticipated by November 30.
